description: A 16 km historical mule track connecting Assam and Bangladesh.
history: Built in the early 1800s by a British administrator, this scenic trail takes you through river crossings, arched bridges, and sweeping valleys, serving as a direct piece of colonial history.

description: An 800-year-old protected forest linked to Khasi religious beliefs.
history: Preserved by the local Khasi tribes, it stands as a living record of their ancient religious beliefs and indigenous conservation practices. The strict rule is that nothing can be taken out of the forest.

description: A rare, two-story natural bridge crafted from living rubber tree roots.
history: A masterpiece of historical bioengineering, the practice of guiding these roots across rivers has been passed down through generations of Khasi and Jaintia tribes for centuries.

description: A hidden river canyon tucked deep within the dense jungles.
history: Located in the South Garo Hills, it offers kayaking through towering, narrow gorges that feel entirely prehistoric and untouched by modern tourism.

description: Fondly known as the 'Mini Dzukou' of Meghalaya.
history: A completely off-the-beaten-path destination featuring rolling green meadows and a breathtaking sea of morning clouds, ideal for early risers and campers.

description: The Whistling Village of the East Khasi Hills.
history: A cultural marvel where every resident is addressed by a specific, unique whistled tune instead of a spoken name—a tradition known as 'Jingrwai Iawbei'.

description: Asia’s second-largest river island, located on the Kynshi River.
history: An untouched and unhurried haven perfect for riverside camping and swimming on sandy inland beaches, separated from the mainland by beautiful rivers.

description: A scenic highland village surrounded by serene lakes.
history: Characterized by rolling hills, pine forests, and cool breezes, it is an idyllic spot for slow travel and experiencing authentic Khasi village hospitality.
Surrounded by thick, untouched greenery, each of the four tiers drops into calm, crystal-clear natural pools perfect for a secluded swim.

description: Walk on narrow bamboo bridges built by locals over deep gorges.
history: Known as the scariest trek in Meghalaya, it requires navigating steep cliff sides on indigenous bamboo structures to reach the massive U Mawryngkhang rock.

description: One of the longest natural caves in Southeast Asia.
history: A rugged subterranean trek located in the East Jaintia Hills. It involves scrambling and muddy crawls through vast caverns and intricate limestone formations.
An iconic sight where water drops dramatically from a high green plateau into a vibrant blue pool, surrounded by the dramatic cliffs of Cherrapunji.

description: Famous for its glass-like, crystal-clear water.
history: Situated near the Bangladesh border, the river is so clear that boats appear to be floating in mid-air above the rocky riverbed. It is a premier spot for boating and camping.
